text.p: British property company Greycoat Plc on Monday criticised a merger approach from smaller rival Moorfield Estates as failing to place a value on Greycoat, lacking a cash alternative and not enhancing shareholder value.

"Moorfield's announcement contains nothing of substance which differs from the outline proposal they delivered last Thursday," Greycoat chairman Michael Beckett said in a statement. Moorfield said earlier that it had developed a proposal "to add value for all shareholders through a strategy of more active management of the assets of Greycoat."
Moorfield's approach comes as Greycoat Plc steels itself for a crucial vote on Friday on a shareholder rebellion aimed at breaking it up.

Beckett said that if Moorfield put forward substantive proposals addressing the issues of how its proposal valued Greycoat and how it might enhance value for Greycoat sharholders, then Greycoat and its advisers would be pleased to consider them.
Moorfield's plan is to merge the two companies by the exchange of shares, valuing both at current net asset value "as established by external professional revaluations."
The plan includes demerging the combined group's Central London portfolio, which would initially be made up of Greycoat's main assets, Embankment Place and 123 Buckingham Palace Road.

A portfolio of investment and development property would be earmarked for "immediate disposal to a major property company" and the remainder of the group's assets would form "an investment, trading and development portfolio."
